overview.problemStatement: Developers must hand-roll Graph API calls for Messenger, Instagram DM, and WhatsApp Cloud, each with its own token model, payloads, webhook signature, and rate-limit signalling, so every consumer re-implements the same error mapping and verification.
overview.proposedSolution: Add a meta feature-flagged module to wirekit exposing MetaClient, FacebookMessenger, InstagramDm, WhatsAppBusiness, SendMessageRequest, MessageAttachment, and WebhookPayload, with Graph error mapping, usage-header backoff, constant-time webhook verification, and normalised inbound events.
overview.targetAudience: Rust developers integrating Meta messaging, including the GIA receptionist, inbox, and social-media agents.
assumptions: Graph API v18.0 remains current for the three surfaces.
Callers supply the app secret, page token, and WhatsApp phone-number id; the crate never reads the environment.
Meta app review, page-token permissions, and WhatsApp business verification are [to be confirmed].
The existing WirekitClient, retry policy, token bucket, Secret type, and WirekitError are reused unchanged.
No external research was performed beyond the repository catalogue and constitution (CON-704).
outOfScope: Facebook Login, feed publishing, ads, and Pages management.
WhatsApp template submission or approval workflows.

userStories.title: Send a Messenger message
userStories.want: to send text or media to a Page-scoped recipient
userStories.benefit: an application can reply where the customer wrote

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given the meta feature and a page token, when send_text runs with a PSID and text, then a POST to /{page-id}/messages carries messaging_type, recipient.id, and the bearer token.
Given a SendMessageRequest with an image attachment, when it is sent, then the body carries an image attachment payload and no plain-text field.

userStories.title: Send an Instagram DM
userStories.want: the same send model for Instagram
userStories.benefit: one client covers both social channels

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given an Instagram-scoped token, when send_text runs, then the request targets the Instagram Graph host and reuses the Messenger request shape.

userStories.title: Send a WhatsApp message or template
userStories.want: text and template sends on WhatsApp Cloud
userStories.benefit: business-initiated messages comply with Meta template rules

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a phone-number id and a template with ordered parameters, when the send runs, then the body carries type template with name, language, and ordered parameters.
Given a plain text message inside the open window, when the send runs, then the body carries type text and the recipient wa_id.

userStories.title: Verify and normalise an inbound webhook
userStories.want: signature verification and a normalised event
userStories.benefit: only authentic payloads reach the application

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a raw body, the app secret, and a correct X-Hub-Signature-256, when verify_and_parse runs, then the HMAC comparison is constant time and the event is returned.
Given a wrong or missing signature, when verification runs, then it fails with an authentication error and nothing is parsed.
Given a subscribe handshake with hub.challenge, when the helper runs, then the challenge is echoed and a mismatched verify token is rejected.
Given an inbound event, when it is normalised, then it exposes the message id as the dedupe key and the surface that produced it.

userStories.title: Fail safely and predictably
userStories.want: consistent Graph error, rate-limit, and secret handling
userStories.benefit: the module never hides a provider error or leaks a token

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a Graph error with code, error_subcode, and fbtrace_id, when the send fails, then WirekitError::Api exposes all three values.
Given a 429 carrying X-Business-Use-Case-Usage, when the request retries, then the policy backs off and the usage value is surfaced.
Given a MetaClient holding a page token and app secret, when it is formatted with Debug, then neither secret appears in the output.
Given a cleartext http base URL, when the client is built, then construction fails with a validation error.

functionalRequirements.text: The crate MUST expose an additive, default-off meta feature that enables no other provider feature.
MetaClient MUST take caller-supplied app secret and tokens, MUST reject a non-HTTPS base URL, and MUST NOT read the environment.
The module MUST provide MetaClient, FacebookMessenger, InstagramDm, WhatsAppBusiness, SendMessageRequest, MessageAttachment, and WebhookPayload.
Messenger and Instagram sends MUST reuse one SendMessageRequest covering text and media.
WhatsApp sends MUST support text and template message types with ordered parameters.
Media upload MUST return an attachment identifier that a subsequent send can reference.
Nested Graph errors MUST map to WirekitError::Api and preserve code, subcode, and trace id.
429 and 5xx MUST flow through the existing retry policy, and X-Business-Use-Case-Usage MUST be surfaced.
Webhook verification MUST use HMAC-SHA256 over raw bytes with a constant-time comparison and MUST fail closed.
The subscription handshake MUST echo hub.challenge and reject a mismatched hub.verify_token.
Normalised inbound events MUST expose the dedupe key and the originating surface.

nonFunctionalRequirements.text: Credentials MUST come from caller config or a secret store and MUST render redacted in Debug (CON-511, CON-519).
Sends MUST be scoped by the page or phone-number identity in the token; a contradicting caller identity MUST be rejected (CON-512).
Provider responses and webhook bodies MUST be validated and bounded before use, with typed errors (CON-515).
All traffic MUST use TLS and a cleartext base URL MUST be rejected (CON-520).
The module MUST compile under forbid(unsafe_code) and deny(missing_docs) like the rest of the crate (CON-201, CON-202).

edgeCases.description: Usage header close to the limit
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: The caller receives the usage value and the retry policy backs off instead of hot-looping.

edgeCases.description: Webhook body above the configured ceiling
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Rejected with a bounds error before parsing.
Parsed into a typed unsupported variant rather than dropped silently.
Rejected locally before any network call.

risks.description: Meta app review and page-token permissions are unconfirmed, so live calls may fail with permission errors.
risks.mitigation: Build against the documented shapes and cover behaviour with a local mock, as m5-gated-integrations did.

risks.description: Graph API version churn changes paths and payloads.
risks.mitigation: One documented version constant, asserted per surface in tests.

risks.description: Instagram and Messenger differ in host and token scope despite a shared payload shape.
risks.mitigation: One request type, two hosts, asserted per surface.
